title: A 1% fee doesn't sound like much. It cost $209,000.
disclaimer: Hypothetical: $100,000 for 30 years at 7% before fees vs 6% after a 1% fee, compounded monthly. Not financial advice.

scenes.narration: A one percent fee sounds tiny. It is not. Guess what one percent actually costs you.
One hundred thousand dollars, invested for thirty years. One fund charges a one percent fee. The other charges nothing. Same money, same market, one difference.
One percent a year, for thirty years. How much does that really cost you? Most people guess way too low.
After thirty years, the no-fee fund leaves you about eight hundred and twelve thousand dollars. The one percent fee fund? Only about six hundred and two thousand.
That one percent quietly took about two hundred and nine thousand dollars. Fees are invisible. The damage is not.

visual.post: Fees are invisible. The damage isn't.
